title: In Sweden, a prime minister can take office with more MPs voting no than yes
body: On 15 October 2026 Sweden’s parliament, the Riksdag, [rejected Magdalena Andersson](https://www.riksdagen.se/en/news/articles/2026/oct/15/no-to-magdalena-andersson-socdem-as-prime_cmsd2ab1134-a03c-4be2-b345-af0aacff33d3en/) as prime minister: 99 MPs voted yes and 248 no, and only her own Social Democrats backed her. Yet she never needed 175 yes votes. A candidate proposed by the Speaker is rejected only if more than half of all 349 members vote no, so MPs who abstain or stay away count as not against. That is how Stefan Löfven became prime minister on 18 January 2019 with 115 yes votes to 153 no, while 77 MPs abstained, and how Magdalena Andersson took office in November 2021 despite 174 no votes, one short of the 175 that would have stopped her. The rule lets a party allow a government to take office without voting for it. The Speaker can make four proposals in all; if all four fail, an extra election must be held within three months.

slides.prompt: In January 2019, Social Democrat leader Stefan Löfven got 115 yes and 153 no votes in Sweden’s parliament. Did he become prime minister?
slides.answer: Yes. It takes 175 no votes to stop a candidate.
slides.detail: 77 members of parliament abstained. Only no votes count against a candidate, who is rejected only if more than half of all 349 members vote no.

slides.alt: Animation on dark blue: the 349 seats of Sweden's parliament as a hemicycle of dots, 99 teal yes and 248 coral no, stamped rejected. A bar of no votes with a gold line at 175, the votes of 2019, 2021 and 2022 approved below the line, four proposal cards and an extra-election ballot box.

slides.prompt: Tap a party to change its vote. Find a way for the candidate to be approved even though more MPs vote no than yes.
slides.takeaway: As long as fewer than 175 vote no, the yes votes can be few: with the Left, Centre and Green parties abstaining, 99 yes beat 173 no. In 2019 Stefan Löfven was approved on 115 yes to 153 no.

slides.question: When Sweden’s parliament votes on a prime minister, how is a member who abstains counted?
options: Not at all: the vote is void
slides.explanation: Only no votes count against a candidate, who is rejected only if more than half of all 349 members, 175 or more, vote no.
